newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks again end higher after breather.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks again end higher after breather.

text.p: Swiss shares shrugged off Tuesday's weakness to close a shortened session firmer with the blue chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) climbing above the psychologically important level of 5,000 points.
"There seems to be just one direction," a dealer said about the market's renewed rise.
"But this may also be a bit dangerous," he warned.
The Swiss bourse had posted four straight record-breaking sessions before Tuesday's correction.
"Everything that comes down is being bought," another trader said.
The SMI ended up 27.6 points, or 0.55 percent, to 5,016.0 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 16.51 points, or 0.52 percent, to 3,167.28.
Bourse volume was 1.55 billion francs, considered good for a shortened session.
The shares were seen profiting from the favourable interest rate environment.
"There is no real alternative to shares," one dealer said.

Actively-traded Roche certificates were in demand. Dealers said the gain of 165 francs to 12,900 francs may stem from derivatives-linked transactions ahead of Friday, when Roche certificates will be traded ex-divided.

Nestle clawed back some of Tuesday's losses, adding 17 francs to 1,819. One dealer said the market took a more favourable view of Nestle's first quarter sales figures after Tuesday's negative reaction.
Cyclicals were generally sought and ABB shares were among the day's biggest winners, adding 29 francs to 1,853.

Among major banks, SBC gained five francs, or 1.54 percent, to 330. The bank's first quarter results are due on Friday and expectations are high, one dealer said. There may have also been switches from CS Group, whose stocks fell 0.25 francs to 167.75, he added.
Shares of Saurer added nine francs to 840 after the company presented a optimistic 1997 outlook, dealers said.
Shares of telecom firm Ascom surged 95 francs to 1,615 after the company said it sold its U.S. unit Nexion to Fujitsu.
